driver: The stable part of a stock held in containers is the money that stays, and a holder moves the money into a new container of the same kind by closing one and opening another on the same day at the same amount, so run-off measured container by container books every move as a loss and a new arrival, and only matching each closing payment to the opening it funded keeps the moved money in the stable part.
driver_concrete: Instant-access members move their savings to each new issue by closing the old account and opening a new one the same day with the same amount, so account cohorts book the moves as run-off; linking each closing payment to the same-day opening deposit it funded keeps that money with the Society and raises the stable balance by about a fifth.
stump: A competent solver estimates run-off on cohorts of accounts open at each start date, the field's own method, and sizes the 2027 hedge too low (a run-off), because a member's move to a new instant-access issue closes one account and opens another and the cohort books it as money gone; following each closing payment into the same-day opening it funded keeps that money and moves the hedge up.

lineage.driver: A step a weekly count takes each time a calendar period turns is not a fixed seasonal share of the count: it is released by the turn from a pool the closing period built, units refused at their first attempt because their qualifying record had not caught up and admitted once the period moves. The share that comes back differs several-fold between the pool's segments and, within the segments that come back at all, falls steeply with the time from the refusal to the turn, since units refused early have mostly moved on by then, steady within each across past turns; so the step is each segment's pool weighed by when within the period each unit was refused, at the segment's own rates. When the closing period's refusals in the segments that come back most fell late in the period, the segments' pools taken whole at their average rates understate the step, and so do the pool taken whole at the pooled rate and every seasonal forecast.

differentiation.task464: task464 v1 fits each unit's response to an external driver and finds the units whose response changed partway through the record; task146 has no response model and no change point: the deciding quantity is the money a savings book keeps, and the step is linking each closing payment to the same-day opening it funded so a member's move between instant-access issues is not booked as run-off.
